summary:
PATHFINDER is a bilingual, evidence-first web platform that helps teams study planetary analogues for future Mars exploration. We developed an interactive Earth–Mars mapping and comparison workflow using real, traceable data from NASA, USGS, and other scientific sources. The platform connects Wadi Hauran in Iraq with Gale Crater on Mars, allowing users to explore native Earth and Mars maps, compare terrain and thermal context, switch between MOLA, THEMIS, and HiRISE layers, upload matched measurements, and generate reproducible scientific reports.
PATHFINDER addresses the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge by turning planetary maps into an explainable mission-planning tool. Its comparison engine only calculates scores when compatible measurements, units, sources, and processing methods are available; missing evidence is clearly identified rather than fabricated. An integrated assistant, Andromeda Iraqi Intelligence, explains similarities, differences, uncertainty, and next steps in Arabic or English. This is important because it makes complex planetary data more accessible while supporting transparent, testable decisions about Earth analogue sites and Mars mission preparation.
details:
PATHFINDER is a bilingual web platform designed to support planetary analogue research and Mars mission preparation. Its main workflow compares an Earth candidate site, Wadi Hauran in Iraq, with a planetary reference site, Gale Crater on Mars, while keeping the two coordinate systems and datasets separate.

Users can explore an interactive Earth map powered by NASA GIBS and related Earth-observation sources, and a native Mars map connected to NASA Mars Trek. The Mars map provides switchable MOLA terrain, HiRISE imagery, and THEMIS daytime and nighttime infrared layers. Users can select a mission profile, upload a structured measurement file, and compare only the properties that have compatible values, units, sources, and processing methods. If a required measurement is missing, PATHFINDER identifies the gap instead of generating a fabricated score.

The platform also includes Andromeda Iraqi Intelligence, a bilingual server-backed assistant that analyzes the selected Earth site, Mars reference, mission context, uploaded measurements, and available source excerpts. It explains similarities, differences, uncertainty, missing evidence, and recommended next steps in English or Iraqi Arabic. The system can then generate a scientific report containing the inputs, comparison axes, sources, methods, results, limitations, and final recommendations. Reports can be printed, saved as PDF, and shared through a reproducible link.

PATHFINDER was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Node.js, tRPC, Leaflet, JSON-based measurement schemas, and a server-side AI integration. The project combines NASA and USGS planetary resources with published Earth geology and topography sources. Its creativity comes from connecting native Earth and Mars maps, real scientific layers, transparent measurement rules, bilingual access, AI explanation, and committee-ready reporting in one workflow. The team considered scientific traceability, coordinate-system differences, data quality, reproducibility, user accessibility, mission relevance, and the risk of overstating what an Earth analogue can represent.
